_notes: What a religious house will do for a parish, and what it asks in return (DESIGN §9.4a). A favour is gated on the standing a priest has built; an ask is answered yes or no, and silence is a no. A favour or an ask with `order` is only done, or only asked, by a house of that order (DESIGN §9.4b); its `effects` are authored here and applied when it is given.

favours.label: Ask them to pray for the parish by name
favours.blurb: They write the parish into the book they read from, and keep it there for a year.
favours.gives: the people know that somebody is praying for them who has never met them

favours.label: Ask for a confessor every Saturday
favours.blurb: A friar drives out for the Saturday hours, indefinitely, and hears the people who will not come to their own pastor.
favours.gives: most of the confessions hour back, and a box that is never empty

favours.label: Take your own retreat at their house
favours.blurb: Eight days in the guest wing at their table, with a director, for nothing.
favours.gives: the canonical retreat, properly made, and the week it takes out of you paid back

favours.label: Ask them to preach a parish mission
favours.blurb: Five nights, a preacher who does this forty weeks a year, and confessions until eleven at night.
favours.gives: a parish that is different in April, and a line at the confessional on the Wednesday

favours.label: Ask them to cover the parish when you are away
favours.blurb: One of theirs says your Masses while you are gone, and they will not take a stipend for it.
favours.gives: a retreat or a fortnight that costs the parish nothing

favours.label: Ask the provincial for a priest of theirs for the parish
favours.blurb: An order man in your rectory for some years: their rule, their habit, their provincial, and your parish.
favours.gives: two blocks of the week back, and a second priest in the house

favours.label: Ask the lector to teach a course in the hall
favours.blurb: Six Thursday nights on the Creed, article by article, from a man who teaches it for a living and preaches it for free.
favours.gives: a parish that knows what it says on Sunday, and a hall full on a weeknight

favours.label: Ask the lector for a written opinion
favours.blurb: Four pages with footnotes that say what you said, in language the chancery cannot call an opinion. It goes in the file with your name beside his.
favours.gives: a stand of yours put on paper by a man the chancery cannot move

favours.label: Ask the friars to run a kitchen out of your hall
favours.blurb: A hot meal on Tuesdays for whoever comes, their brother in charge, their volunteers, and a line down the block, indefinitely.
favours.gives: the parish's poor in the parish's own hall, and a city that knows whose hall it is

favours.label: Ask the friary to take the parish's winter
favours.blurb: The coal fund, the Christmas baskets, the families you have been carrying on the parish's money: theirs until Easter, and they will not hear of being paid back.
favours.gives: a winter the parish's books do not have to carry, and the families carried anyway

favours.label: Ask for a place at their school for a family of the parish
favours.blurb: A boy who could not have gone, in a blazer on the first Monday of September: the tuition halved by the headmaster, the rest found somewhere.
favours.gives: one family of the parish that will never forget it, and the ones who hear

favours.label: Ask for a place at their table
favours.blurb: Dinner at the priory on Thursdays at six, from now on: the prior at the head, the argument of the week, and nobody asking about the parish unless you bring it up.
favours.gives: a chair at a table, once a week, for a man who has no community and was not supposed to need one

asks.label: Their chaplain is ill
asks.blurb: They need a priest for the community Mass four mornings a week until their own man is back on his feet.
asks.costs: an hour a day for a couple of months, and the drive

asks.label: A collection for their missions
asks.blurb: One Sunday, a second collection, and a friar to speak at every Mass about a house in Guatemala.
asks.costs: a Sunday of the plate, and the people who mind being asked

asks.label: Their novena in your church
asks.blurb: Nine evenings of their devotion in your church, with their preacher and their people, some of whom are not yours.
asks.costs: nine evenings of the church, and the sacristan

asks.label: Back them with the chancery
asks.blurb: The diocese wants their property for a school site and they would like a pastor of the diocese to say, in writing, what the house is worth.
asks.costs: a letter with your name on it, in a file, against the chancery

asks.label: Take a man of theirs for a while
asks.blurb: One of their young men needs parish experience and a room, and they are asking you rather than the chancery.
asks.costs: a room, a summer, and a man who is not yours to form

asks.label: Their lector wants your hall for a disputation
asks.blurb: A public argument, Thursday night, their lector against a professor from the state university, on whether God can be known: two hundred chairs, a moderator, and whatever gets said.
asks.costs: the hall for a night, the chairs, and whatever your name is under by Friday

asks.label: The Transitus in your church
asks.blurb: The evening of the third of October: the friars keep the death of Francis by candlelight, with the readings and the Canticle, and they would like to keep it in your church because theirs is too small for who comes.
asks.costs: the church for an October evening, the sacristan, and the neighbours' parking

asks.label: A table at their school's dinner
asks.blurb: The annual dinner for the school's fund, a table of ten, and the parish's name on the programme beside the families who send their boys there.
asks.costs: a table's worth of the parish's money, and an evening in a jacket
